episodes.212153: Deep moisture pooled across the lower Mid-Atlantic during the afternoon and evening of the 25th ahead of a slow-moving cold front situated near the Ohio River, with precipitable water values reaching into the 1.8 to 1.9 inch range across the Southside area of Virginia per Storm Prediction Center Meso-analysis. Abundant daytime heating allowed CAPE values to reach in excess of 1,500 J/kg during the evening. A line of slow-moving thunderstorms developed along a nearly-stationary surface trough that extended from Carroll County through central Halifax and Charlotte Counties, with multiple cells observed training along this boundary. The heaviest rain was observed within the Polecat Creek and Miry Creek basins, where nearly 5.5 inches fell within a 3-hour period. Multiple cells were estimated by radar to be producing rainfall rates of 3 to 5 inches per hour. Cells began to develop over the basins at around 6:00 pm EDT, with training reaching a maximum at around 8:00 pm EDT. Despite dry antecedent conditions with D3: Extreme Drought highlighted for all of Halifax County by the U.S. Drought Monitor, MRMS FLASH data estimated the rainfall reached the 200-year Average Recurrence Interval ceiling for a 3-hour duration along a east-west strip within the west-central portion of the county, with rainfall totals reaching 150 percent of the 3-hour Flash Flood Guidance. CREST Unit Streamflow ranged from 350 to 650 cfs per mi^2 during the storm.
episodes.212164: A decaying thunderstorm produced isolated wind damage in the northern portions of the city of Florence. Multiple rounds of heavy rainfall led to flash flooding in Marshall, Jackson, and Cullman Counties in Northeastern Alabama, flooding roads and causing them to become impassable.
episodes.212313: A line of thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front during the afternoon hours on Tuesday (5/26).  The strongest storm produced wind damage across portions of north-central Wisconsin.
episodes.212335: Thunderstorms occurred over the eastern half of the CWA, generating winds to 63 mph and rainfall over a half inch.
episodes.212354: Scattered thunderstorms developed across southwest Minnesota very early in the morning and travelled northeast farther into Minnesota. One storm quickly strengthened and produced quarter size hail in southern Kandiyohi County, then weakened below severe limits before it reached Willmar.
episodes.212366: On May 25th, height falls ahead of an incoming trough and surface heating allowed for weak instability to build in across southwest Idaho. Strong south-southwesterly winds ahead of an incoming cold front allowed for a hot, well-mixed boundary layer and subsequent inverted-V temperature profiles. Shear was weak but sufficient to support a multicell with a damaging wind threat. Severe winds resulting in numerous trees down across the area.
episodes.212616: Difluence ahead of an incoming shortwave interacted with ample moisture across west Texas and southeast New Mexico, allowing for showers and thunderstorms to develop across the area during the morning of the 26th. The biggest issue during the morning was training thunderstorms which, combined with heavy rainfall, yielded flash flooding for numerous locations. Later that evening, storms redeveloped in southeast New Mexico and moved into portions of west Texas. Large hail and strong winds were observed with these storms.
episodes.212617: Difluence ahead of an incoming shortwave interacted with ample moisture across west Texas and southeast New Mexico, allowing for showers and thunderstorms to develop across the area during the morning of the 26th. The biggest issue during the morning was training thunderstorms which, combined with heavy rainfall, yielded flash flooding for numerous locations. Later that evening, storms redeveloped in southeast New Mexico and moved into portions of west Texas. Large hail and strong winds were observed with these storms.
episodes.212669: A weak upper level disturbance moved over the area from morning into the afternoon hours. Lift from this feature along with a very moist atmosphere created scattered thunderstorms across the region. Although most storms brought brief heavy rainfall, a couple of storms became severe producing severe wind gusts.
episodes.212751: Showers and thunderstorms brought wet road conditions on May 26th to Highway 50 in El Dorado County. Just east of Ice House Road, a vehicle veered off the roadway and into the American River. Rainfall amounts of 0.15-0.25 were observed at the time of the incident. There were two fatalities and two injuries with this.
episodes.213032: A similar environment to 5/24 took shape during the afternoon of 5/25, continuing into the late evening. Seasonal instability brought summertime pulse convection that was slow moving with efficient rain rates as PWAT's neared 2. This led to a couple instances of flash flooding in southern Lancaster County, SC early in the afternoon before bringing a couple more instances later in the evening near Augusta GA.
episodes.213034: Weak upper ridging persisted across the forecast area on 5/26, but seasonable instability, PWAT's near 2, and enhanced moisture convergence led to scattered thunderstorm development during the afternoon and evening hours. One isolated severe storm in Aiken County produced tree damage before training, slow moving convection produced two instances of flash flooding in Orangeburg County.
episodes.213050: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front moving across the southern half of the Northland during the late afternoon and early evening hours of the 26th. A few of the storms were strong to marginally severe producing mainly hail to 1 inch in diameter. Some minor damage from thunderstorm winds was also reported.
episodes.213051: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front moving across the southern half of the Northland during the late afternoon and early evening hours of the 26th. A few of the storms were strong to marginally severe producing mainly hail to 1.25 inches in diameter.
episodes.213052: Thunderstorms developed across parts of northwest and west central Minnesota during the afternoon hours on May 26, with one report of quarter size hail in Hubbard County, MN. Other storms that carried stronger radar signatures may have been severe, however they remained in very rural areas and reports were not received.
episodes.213361: An upper level low over Texas began to lift northeast on May 25th, leading to widespread showers and thunderstorm affecting East Tennessee and the western North Carolina. Heavy rains noted in East Tennessee lead to several roads being flooded in Sevier county, along with a mudslide in the Gatlinburg area, as well as some flooding of small streams and flooded roadways in the northern parts of Hamilton county.
episodes.213362: An upper level low over Texas began to lift northeast on May 25th, leading to widespread showers and thunderstorm affecting East Tennessee and the western North Carolina. Heavy rains noted in western North Carolina produced isolated flooding issues in Clay county.
episodes.213592: An EF-0 tornado briefly touched down near Parrish in Manatee County as a developing thunderstorm interacted with intersecting sea breeze and convective outflow boundaries resulting in a brief spin-up. Elsewhere, easterly sea breeze afternoon convection produced a severe wind gust near Punta Gorda in Charlotte County.
episodes.213616: Scattered thunderstorms occurred ahead of a frontal boundary on May 22-25. However, on May 25, a mesoscale convective system developed west of the area and enhanced the low level wind field.  This resulted in two tornadoes across the tri-state area. One tornado affected the Villa Tasso area in Walton county in Florida, and the other tornado affected Houston and Henry counties in Alabama.  Both tornadoes were rated EF1.
episodes.213666: An upper-level trough brought in enough moisture and instability to produce isolated severe thunderstorms over Central MT. Dry air at the surface helped storms produce severe wind gusts.
episodes.213675: Heavy downpours occurred across central MS and south MS during the afternoon hours of May 25. These downpours lead to multiple roads to be flooded and one fatality.
episodes.213754: By the evening on May 25, the environment over northeast Nebraska became favorable for thunderstorm development along a weak zone of surface convergence and near the nose of a developing low-level jet. Overall forcing for ascent remained weak, and deep-layer bulk shear was marginal, generally around 25 knots. However, instability was plentiful, with a corridor of 2,000 to 2,500 J/kg of MUCAPE extending into the region. Driven by this strong thermodynamic environment, a minimally organized cluster of thunderstorms initiated across north-central Nebraska during the late afternoon before drifting eastward into northeast Nebraska through the evening hours. Two public reports of hail measured at 1.00 inch in diameter were reported in Oakdale, NE at 8:19 PM CST and another 7 miles southwest of Clearwater, NE at 9:15 PM CST. A measured thunderstorm wind gust of 61 mph was reported near Neligh, NE at 8:29 PM CST.
episodes.213777: During the evening hours on May 26th, a couple strong to severe storms produced penny to quarter sized hail in portions of Mower County.
episodes.213798: Widespread, slow-moving showers and storms trained over the same areas and resulted in locally heavy rainfall and scattered flash flooding across central and eastern Virginia on May 25.
episodes.213799: Slow-moving showers and storms resulted in locally heavy rainfall and localized flash flooding across central Virginia on May 26.
episodes.213963: An upper shortwave trough moved across Texas and generated thunderstorms. Some storms formed along a dryline over the western edge of South-Central Texas. Other storms formed east of the dryline in a conditionally unstable, moist airmass. Storms produced all severe hazards and locally heavy rain.
episodes.213969: The dynamic breakup front finally arrived at the lower reaches of the Yukon River across the Yukon Delta by late May 2026. This resulted in severe, cascading flood impacts for multiple communities as the high water made it's way to the mouth of the Yukon River, inundating the coastal delta.
episodes.214011: An upper level low moving southeast into southwest Oregon produced numerous thunderstorms. Severe winds were measured across central Jackson County with one of the thunderstorms.
episodes.214067: A few thunderstorms produced a few reports large hail.
episodes.214083: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed across western North Carolina during the afternoon and evening. A series of thunderstorm cells became anchored on the slopes of Bearwallow Mountain in Henderson County, resulting in torrential rainfall that lasted for a couple of hours, resulting in flash flooding.
episodes.214405: A weak wave in northwest flow aloft enhanced the low-level jet into southeast South Dakota with moisture and better deep-layer shear arriving by late day near a weak frontal boundary. With mixed-layer instability from 1500-2200 J/kg and marginally supportive deep layer shear of 40-45 kts, isolated supercells developed with mainly hail from stronger cells up to 2 inches in diameter.
episodes.214416: Easterly sea breeze afternoon convection produced gusty marine winds over Tampa Bay.
episodes.214760: Strong instability and weak wind shear led to scattered multi-cell thunderstorms across central and southern Oklahoma on the afternoon and evening of the 26th. One of these storms produced wind damage near Hobart in Kiowa County.

The tornado initially touched down just north of U.S. 84 near Cowarts in Houston County, damaging trees and outbuildings. A pool screen was damaged at a home along Omussee Road, with additional tree and minor damage to homes. The tornado damaged the WDHN television station as it crossed Highway 52, breaking windows and damaging the roof. The tornado continued north-northeast downing trees and causing minor structural damage before moving into Henry County at County Road 22 and Buckhead Drive. The most severe damage was along County Road 15 where two homes were heavily damage. One home was destroyed. This home separated from the concrete foundation, slid, and then collapsed. The damage is consistent with an EF1 tornado with maximum winds of approximately 105 mph.

Chatham Road was observed flooded and impassible as heavy rain caused Polecat Creek to rise out of its banks several inches deep across the roadway surface.  No damage was observed to the road, which was reopened to traffic after the flooding receded.

Multiple sources reported significant flash flooding developed across northeast Henderson County after 4 to 7 inches of rain fell on the slopes of Bearwallow Mountain in just a couple of hours. The main impact was to Clear Creek and its tributaries, including Puncheon Camp Creek, Cox Creek, and Laurel Fork. A culvert washed out underneath a section of Highway 74 in the Gerton community, forcing closure of the road for a few days. A section of Bearwallow Rd was also washed out in the Edneyville area. Multiple other roads were inundated and closed throughout the area, while multiple culverts under private driveways and some small bridges were reportedly washed out or damaged. A few homes were briefly isolated due to washed out culverts or flooded roads. The high flows on Clear Creek, combined with subsequent heavy rainfall in the Mud Creek basin resulted in the French Broad River rising to bankfull in Flecther and vicinity.
At 540pm MST, Idaho Power mesonet station W3T7 measured a 58 mph wind gust.

No damage was observed to the roadway, which was open to traffic after the water receded.

The NWS River Watch team reported that the Alakanuk Slough jammed at its mouth, causing minor flooding that primarily impacted the south riverbank. Roads leading to the airport were covered in water by Tuesday afternoon (May 26th). However, because the upstream Yukon River was largely clear of ice, the flood threat diminished quickly, and water levels dropped 2 feet below bankfull by Tuesday night.

Public report of JBS Pkwy flooded between Pearl and Trunk streets in Odessa with cars  stalled out. The total time of occurrence is partially estimated from radar. The cost of damages is also estimated.

Public report of an accident involving a truck with trailer caused by hydroplaning.  The total time of occurrence of heavy rainfall leading to ponding/flash flooding is partially estimated from radar. The cost of damages is estimated.
Public reports and pictures of flood water over roads at the intersection of FM1788 and I-20.  The total time of occurrence is partially estimated from radar. No damage was reported.

Upton County Sheriffs Office reports flooding on US Hwy 67 between Rankin and  McCamey and have closed the road. The total time of occurrence is partially estimated from radar. No damage was reported.

The National Weather Service conducted a damage survey of a line of thunderstorms that impacted portions of southern Guadalupe County during the late night hours of May 26th. The survey team found damage that supported the existence of a short-lived EF-1 tornado. A tornadic debris signature was seen on radar just north of where the most extensive damage was surveyed. The tornado may have started just east of Linne Rd. The most significant damage occurred north of Kunde Rd. with widespread tree damage surveyed. The circulation continued east where more tree damage was noted. The tornado may have traveled farther southeast, but the team was not able to access the property where there may have been additional damage. The damage was rated as EF-1 with maximum winds estimated at 105 mph.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Vigo Park measured a severe wind gust of 77 mph.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Jayton measured severe wind gusts from 1412 CST through 1413 CST. A peak gust of 62 mph was measured at 1413 CST.
A thunderstorm produced half dollar size hail on Hwy 55 south of Laguna.
Dime to penny size hail reported near Calhoun.
West-northwest thunderstorm outflow winds reached a peak of 38 mph with a gust of 61 mph at the Rogue Valley International Airport at 155 pm pst.
Half dollar to ping pong sized hail fell near Beaver and Wolverine Way in Tetonia.  A broken skylight and windshield reported.
A thunderstorm produced quarter size hail in Pearsall.
The Lambert MT-200 DOT site (MTLBT) measured a 63 mph wind gust.
Flooding was reported in Colonial Heights via mPING.

A tornado briefly touched down just west of U.S. Hwy 301, where the resident of a home along Loch Ness Gln witnessed damage to the backyard fence. The resident reported that the tornado lifted shortly thereafter, while another area resident witnessed debris being lofted in an open field just to the north prior to the tornado lifting. No additional damage or reports were received.
An NWS employee reported flooding on Courthouse Road. Cars needed to drive on the center line to get through.
A thunderstorm produced quarter size hail in Fredericksburg.
Report received via mPING.
VDOT reported high standing water over the road, causing delays, on Church Road near Squirrel Level Road.
ASOS site KPGD Punta Gorda Airport reported a 70 mph wind gust.
Thunderstorm winds downed trees and power lines in Antigo.
Saluda County EM reported flooding at the corner of Batesburg Highway and Bouknight  Ferry Road. EM sent photos of water pooling  around trailers.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts measured at 60 mph by a storm chaser five miles east of Pearsall.

VDOT reported standing water on the I-295 Eastbound ramp (Exit 9A) at mile marker 0 in the City of Hopewell.
An mPING report indicated flooding.

The National Weather Service received reports of a brief tornado across rural portions of Maverick County several miles north of Quemado. Several storm chasers had reported that a funnel cloud moved across US Highway 277 and briefly fully condensed to the ground just east of the highway for a short time. Small broken tree branches were noted off the highway, supporting EF-0 damage. Maximum winds were estimated at 65 mph.
Social media images from the Prince George Police Department showed flooding in the Pine Ridge community, with water almost onto the hood of a sedan.

Hail report from 13 NNE Van Horn. A NWS storm spotter sent a report of quarter sized hail observed while on a walking trail off of Hwy 54.  The total time of occurrence is partially estimated from radar.
A thunderstorm produced ping pong ball size hail on Hwy 85 southeast of Pearsall.
The Lieutenant Run Creek at Bollingbrook in Petersburg rapidly rose from around 5 feet  to 10.96 feet in one hour between 4 and 5 PM EST. Minor flood stage is 10.5 feet.
A trained spotter at 12SSE Sprole estimated 60 mph wind gusts, and reported trees damaged by lightning.
A thunderstorm produced ping pong ball size hail in Quemado.
A video was shared via social media showing water, several inches deep, completely covering a yard in Hopewell.
A portion of a sheet metal roof was ripped off a structure and a nearby tree was knocked down as well.
A thunderstorm produced quarter size hail in Normandy.
Size was estimated to be around quarter-sized, but the appearance of the hail in photos suggested slightly larger.

Broadcast Media relayed information from California Highway Patrol regarding an accident that occurred on May 26th around 4 PM PDT. Showers and thunderstorms brought wet road conditions on May 26th to Highway 50 in El Dorado County. Just east of Ice House Road, a vehicle veered off the roadway and into the American River. Rainfall amounts of 0.15-0.25 were observed at the time of the incident. A 35 year old woman died at the scene, and a 5 year old boy died in the hospital as a result of the accident. An 11 year old boy and a 41 year old man were injured from this accident.
